MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which number is written in words as "seven thousand and eight"? (1 mark)
   A. 70,008
   B. 708
   C. 8,008
   D. 7,008

2. Which of these is a multiple of 6? (1 mark)
   A. 53
   B. 54
   C. 55
   D. 56

3. Which of these is a multiple of 3? (1 mark)
   A. 53
   B. 52
   C. 50
   D. 51

4. Estimate 4,368 + 2,547 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 6,920
   B. 6,910
   C. 7,015
   D. 6,930

5. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 3,425 + 2,318? (1 mark)
   A. 0
   B. 3
   C. 2
   D. 1

6. Estimate 2,694 + 3,158 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 5,860
   B. 5,840
   C. 5,850
   D. 5,952

7. Work out 5,432 − 2,718. (1 mark)
   A. 3,326
   B. 2,714
   C. 2,614
   D. 2,724

8. Work out 7,000 − 3,456. (1 mark)
   A. 3,544
   B. 4,456
   C. 3,554
   D. 3,444

9. What is 15 × 40? (1 mark)
   A. 6,000
   B. 600
   C. 55
   D. 60

10. Estimate 27 × 13 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 200
   B. 300
   C. 3,000
   D. 400

11. Work out 25 × 16. (1 mark)
   A. 175
   B. 410
   C. 390
   D. 400

12. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 4 × 6 = 24? (1 mark)
   A. 24 ÷ 4 = 6
   B. 24 ÷ 4 = 4
   C. 24 ÷ 24 = 4
   D. 6 ÷ 4 = 24

13. What is 38 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 8 remainder 3
   B. 6 remainder 8
   C. 7 remainder 3
   D. 7 remainder 4

14. What is 900 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 10
   C. 9
   D. 90

15. Change 6 2/3 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 8/3
   B. 21/3
   C. 18/3
   D. 20/3

16. Change 23/6 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 4 5/6
   B. 3 6/6
   C. 5 3/6
   D. 3 5/6

17. In the fraction 3/5, what does the numerator 3 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many equal parts the whole has
   B. The number of wholes
   C. How many of the equal parts are taken
   D. The size of each part in centimetres

18. Which is the largest number: 2.5, 2.05, 2.55, 2.505? (1 mark)
   A. 2.55
   B. 2.505
   C. 2.05
   D. 2.5

19. Which decimal is the same as 3/4? (1 mark)
   A. 3.4
   B. 0.3
   C. 0.75
   D. 0.34

20. Write 3/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 3.0
   B. 0.3
   C. 0.13
   D. 0.03

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Round 47, 342 and 995 to the nearest ten. (3 marks)

22. Explain why 0.5 is greater than 0.45 even though 0.45 has more digits. (3 marks)

23. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5,000, 4,750, 4,500, 4,250. (3 marks)

24. Explain the difference between a factor and a multiple, using the number 6 as an example. (3 marks)

25. Sort these fractions into proper, improper and mixed: 3/8, 11/5, 2 1/2, 9/9, 7/10. (4 marks)

26. A trader has 800 eggs. Each crate holds 100 eggs. How many crates are needed? (2 marks)

27. A rectangle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction is shaded and what fraction is not shaded? (2 marks)

28. Tabitha has 2,450 eggs. She gets 3,875 more. How many eggs does she have now? (3 marks)

29. A water tank holds 1,000 litres. Each day the family uses 125 litres. Write the amount left after 1, 2 and 3 days. (3 marks)

30. Divide 450 by 100 and give the remainder. Explain what the remainder means. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 7,008
   seven thousand and eight: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 7,008.

2. B — 54
   54 = 6 × 9, so 54 is a multiple of 6.

3. D — 51
   51 = 3 × 17, so 51 is a multiple of 3.

4. A — 6,920
   4,368 rounds to 4,370 and 2,547 rounds to 2,550. 4,370 + 2,550 = 6,920.

5. D — 1
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 3,425 + 2,318 needs 1 regrouping.

6. C — 5,850
   2,694 rounds to 2,690 and 3,158 rounds to 3,160. 2,690 + 3,160 = 5,850.

7. B — 2,714
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 5,432 − 2,718 = 2,714. Check: 2,714 + 2,718 = 5,432.

8. A — 3,544
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 7,000 − 3,456 = 3,544. Check: 3,544 + 3,456 = 7,000.

9. B — 600
   15 × 4 = 60, then × 10 gives 600.

10. B — 300
   27 rounds to 30 and 13 rounds to 10. 30 × 10 = 300.

11. D — 400
   25 × 6 = 150 and 25 × 10 = 250. 150 + 250 = 400.

12. A — 24 ÷ 4 = 6
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 4 × 6 = 24, we know 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

13. C — 7 remainder 3
   5 × 7 = 35 and 38 − 35 = 3. So 38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. Check: 7 × 5 + 3 = 38.

14. C — 9
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 900 ÷ 100 = 9.

15. D — 20/3
   6 × 3 = 18 and 18 + 2 = 20. The denominator stays 3, so the answer is 20/3.

16. D — 3 5/6
   23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 5/6, so 23/6 = 3 5/6.

17. C — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 3/5 it says that 3 parts are taken.

18. A — 2.55
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The largest number is 2.55.

19. C — 0.75
   3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75.

20. B — 0.3
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 3/10 = 0.3.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: 50, 340 and 1,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rounding. 995 goes up to 1,000 because the ones digit is 5.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.5 = 0.50. Comparing tenths, 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths, so 0.50 is greater than 0.45. The number of digits does not decide the size.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for writing 0.5 as 0.50, 1 mark for comparing tenths, 1 mark for the conclusion.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4,000, 3,750, 3,500 (rule: subtract 250)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three numbers.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: A factor divides a number exactly: the factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6. A multiple is found by multiplying: the multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Proper: 3/8 and 7/10. Improper: 11/5 and 9/9. Mixed: 2 1/2.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group and 1 mark for placing all five correctly.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8 crates
   Working / marking points: 800 ÷ 100 = 8. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the unit.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: 5/12 is shaded and 7/12 is not shaded.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 5/12 and 1 mark for 12 − 5 = 7, so 7/12.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6,325 eggs
   Working / marking points: Ones 0 + 5 = 5; tens 5 + 7 = 12 write 2 carry 1; hundreds 4 + 8 + 1 = 13 write 3 carry 1; thousands 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. 1 mark for method, 1 for regrouping, 1 for answer with unit.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 875 litres, 750 litres, 625 litres
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct amount.

30. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4 remainder 50. There are 4 whole hundreds in 450 and 50 is left over.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4, 1 mark for remainder 50, 2 marks for the explanation.
